walkthroughs.body_html: Muhammad was born in Mecca in 570 CE. He worked as a merchant, known for being honest and trustworthy. At about age 40, he began receiving revelations from God (Allah) through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) — these became the Quran.

Muhammad faced opposition in Mecca, so in 622 CE he and his followers moved to Medina. This journey is called the Hijra and marks the start of the Muslim calendar. In Medina he built the first Muslim community.

By the time Muhammad died in 632 CE, much of Arabia had become Muslim. Within a century, Islam spread across the Middle East, North Africa and into Asia and Europe. Today there are about 1.9 billion Muslims worldwide.

mcqs.q: What is the problem of evil?
options: It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
It is the question of whether evil people will go to hell.
If God is all-loving, all-knowing and all-powerful, why does evil and suffering exist? Logically, all four cannot be true together without explanation.
Atonement means Jesus apologised to humans for being born divine.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between act and rule utilitarianism?
options: It is the question of whether the devil really exists.
Act utilitarianism is about action movies and rule utilitarianism is about laws.
Act and rule utilitarianism are basically the same approach.

Act utilitarianism judges each individual action by its consequences; rule utilitarianism follows rules that, if generally adopted, would produce the most good — sacrificing case-by-case calculation for predictability and fairness.
